done.summary:
All nine WP1 acceptance tests are permanent pytests in turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp1_data_identity.py: 26 tests, all passing. The full suite (`turbotab/core turbotab/server`) has 854 passed, and the frontend check (tsc, eslint, 152 vitest) is green.

What changed:
- **Dates (MA-05).** A shared date reader is new (turbotab/core/dates.py). At ingest, a date column that reads the same month-first and day-first stays text, with a warning. A new `ambiguous_dates` finding shows three example rows under each reading and offers month-first or day-first as a repair. The structure stage now reads that answer, so after "month first" the quarterly visits read 91 days apart, exactly like the ISO copy.
- **Combining order (MA-03).** Records are ordered by numbers, by dates (including text like "Mar 3, 2021"), or by a declared order of text levels (`RepeatSpec.levels`). Undated records are never first or last and are counted in the receipt. If the time column cannot order the records, the answer is refused with exits, and the stage refuses too as a backstop. `ordered_by` now says "file order" whenever the named column ordered nothing.
- **Per-column combining (MA-14, B21, B22).** Each column is combined by what it holds: a constant keeps its value, a code takes its most frequent value (or its baseline under change), an amount follows the method. The receipt lists every column that varied, with its rule, and a column's rule can be overridden. First and last now mean the value at that record for the outcome too. Averaging a two-level outcome is refused.
- **Turning a feature table (MA-04).** Columns are split into the label, feature annotations (m/z, RT, IDs; kept in `features.parquet`) and samples. Numeric gene IDs stay feature names. A column that does not move with the samples is refused, with a `set_feature_table` exit. The orientation and aggregation previews now call the stage's own functions.
- **Categorical declaration (MA-15).** A `set_categorical` decision makes a column enter as indicators. The roles stage proposes it for whole-number columns with 3–10 values and for known NHANES coded variables.
- **Spellings and infinities (MA-16, MA-18, B18).** New repair families: text read as numbers (every unparsed spelling named with its count), a separate below-detection-limit family, infinite values, and date reading. Codes are now blanked before the kJ conversion and are compared safely on text columns.
- **Ingest (MA-17, C14).** Unambiguous decimal commas are read as numbers. Integers past 2**53 that would be read as doubles stay text. Excel uses the CSV reader's missing-value tokens. Summaries are computed over finite values, with infinities counted in a new `n_infinite` field.
- **Flow counts (MA-19, D16).** A row with no value, or one a by-sex screen cannot screen, leaves on its own line by default (`ExclusionRule.missing`). The range line now counts only rows in range.
- **Group keys (C12).** "007", "07" and "7" are kept apart.

done.summary:
Under inference, the linear family's coefficient table now gets its intervals from a new module, /Users/nhedglin/tabular-ml-lab/.claude/worktrees/wf_e4f6ae8a-38e-2/turbotab/core/models/inference.py.

(1) Which rows belong together is decided from the grain answer, the identifier roles and the analysis rows themselves, not from how the seal grouped them. So "I don't know" (undetermined) and "one row each" while an ID repeats (abandoned) are both clustered by that ID, and a concern says why. A missing ID counts as a unit of its own, exactly as the split maps it (closes A18).

(2) When rows repeat, the intervals use CR2 standard errors with Bell–McCaffrey Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. One engine serves OLS, logistic and multinomial models, and it never builds an n_g × n_g matrix. Below the seal's 8-unit floor, the table keeps the estimates and reports no interval or p-value. The refusal and its exits are recorded: combine each unit's rows into one, or a mixed model or GEE (not yet available). A concern names G whenever G < 30. If the degrees of freedom would cost too much to compute, the intervals fall back to t(G−1) and the caption says so.

(3) Independent OLS rows get HC3 standard errors on t(n−p). A Breusch–Pagan (Koenker) check says so when the spread is not constant and that changes the standard errors by at least 10%.

(4) Separation in a logistic model is found by linear programming (Konis), the separating column is named, and the table becomes Firth's penalized fit with profile-likelihood intervals and likelihood-ratio p-values. With repeated rows as well, it keeps the Firth estimates and refuses intervals.

The API gains Coefficient.se and Coefficient.df, and FittedModel.inference (estimator, covariance, caption, clusters, refusal, exits). The Results show the caption, and the fit stage version went from 3 to 4.

Before I built on the CR2 engine, I checked it independently. It matches the definition written out with n×n matrices to 1e-15, statsmodels' HC2 for one-row clusters, the Imbens–Kolesár closed form exactly (both SE and df), and statsmodels' own clustered sandwich for OLS, logistic and multinomial. I also used a calibration simulation to choose the method: CR2 with these degrees of freedom held type-I error at 0.030–0.062 for G = 6–20. On the same data, the app's old normal-based intervals gave 0.09–0.25, and CR1 with t(G−1) still gave 0.07–0.16. The acceptance tests are in /Users/nhedglin/tabular-ml-lab/.claude/worktrees/wf_e4f6ae8a-38e-2/turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp2_intervals.py, and the independent reference computations are in references.py next to it.

Firth estimates match an independent optimizer (rtol 1e-5). In the 2×2 case, Firth equals the Haldane +½ log odds ratio (1e-9). Profile bounds and p-values match the definition recomputed with a generic optimizer (1e-5). Must-not-fire: 0 of 50 non-separated datasets flagged, and their Wald CIs equal statsmodels'. Separation with clustering keeps the Firth estimates and refuses intervals. The real fit stage reports separated == ['exposed'].

tests.detail: 847 passed in 146.78s, on the final code before commit. The WP2 acceptance file alone takes about 54s; its longest test is the 2 × 1,000-replicate real-stage Monte Carlo (about 25s). Frontend: npm ci then npm run check passed (tsc, eslint, 152 vitest tests including the generated-types drift check). The pre-commit gates were all green.

deviations: Test 3, first part: the package asks that at G = 10 the half-width over SE equal t(9) = 2.262 with the caption 'cluster-robust, G = 10, t(9)'. The engine instead uses CR2 with Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom at every G. That is the method the package's own recommendation names below 30–50 clusters, and the one Cameron & Miller call 'the best methods use the CR2VE and T(v*)'. Their 'at a minimum … T(G − 1)' is the floor, not the target. Evidence: in my calibration CR1 with t(G−1) still rejected 0.10–0.12 at G = 8–12 (the skeptic measured 0.12–0.15), while CR2 with these df gave 0.036–0.062. The test asserts the nearest honest version: use_t holds, half-width/SE equals the t quantile at each row's reported df, and at G = 10 (5 against 5 clusters) that df is 8 from the Imbens–Kolesár closed form, giving 2.306 ≥ 2.262. The caption names CR2, G = 10 and Bell–McCaffrey. t(G−1) appears only as a stated fallback when the df computation would exceed its cost budget, and that path is tested too.

Test 1 runs 1,000 replicates instead of 400. This is stricter: at 400 replicates (Monte Carlo SE 0.011) even statsmodels' clustered reference landed at 0.930, so the 0.93 bound barely told the two apart. Measured 0.939 against a reference of 0.937.
The worktree was created from main (f5e935c), not turbotab-next. Because it was clean, I reset the worktree branch to turbotab-next (88d22aa) before starting, so the commit sits directly on 88d22aa.

Files outside the models directory that I touched, each kept small. turbotab/core/stages/modeling.py: about 20 lines in fit_stage's coefficient block — it reads the candidate unit columns, resolves the clusters once, calls family.inference(), and stores model['inference']; the old cluster concern was removed. turbotab/core/stages/__init__.py: fit stage version 3 → 4, so cached fits with the old z-based intervals are recomputed. turbotab/core/models/artifacts.py: new optional fields. turbotab/server/openapi.json and turbotab/frontend/src/api/generated.ts were regenerated. Frontend mocks (m1-stages.ts) and derive.test.ts got the new required fields set to null. Coefficients.tsx and Results.tsx: one caption expression each, so the on-screen line and the saved figure name the covariance. docs/turbotab-next/M1_CONTRACT.md: the fit artifact description. Expect merge conflicts with other packages that touch fit_stage or the API schema (WP4 in particular); openapi.json and generated.ts should be regenerated rather than hand-merged.

The exits have no attached decision ('decision': null): unit and aggregation changes are refused once the seal is drawn, and the mixed-model or GEE exit points to WP12. Turning these into executable decisions belongs to the routing packages.
Intervals are still computed on the training rows. Ruling 3 (inference estimates from all eligible rows) is ME-12, which is WP8, not this package.

Separation detection covers binary outcomes only. Multinomial separation is not detected. Firth combined with clustered rows refuses intervals, because there is no standard sound interval for that combination.

The covariance is chosen by the engine and stated in the caption. There is no user decision offering classical, HC3, CR1 with t(G−1), CR2, or a wild cluster bootstrap with 'customary' and 'sound' labels (north star 5). That is a routing change, listed in the inbox.

done.summary:
The within-sex energy residual no longer creates a nutrient effect out of sex. Before the fix, the stratified residual fitted N ~ E within each level and added back that level's own mean nutrient, so the adjusted nutrient carried the difference between levels. When sex was not a predictor, a nutrient with no effect reached p = 2.9e-106, with r(fat_adj, sex) = 0.58. That baseline was reproduced on HEAD with the skeptic's B-skeptic/s1_strata.py.

The adjustment within level s is now N_adj = N − b_s(E − Ē_s) − N̄_s + N̂(cohort mean E). Every level gets the same constant, as NUTRITION_PACK line 446 says. On the fitting rows, N_adj is therefore uncorrelated with energy and with the strata column, both pooled and within levels, whether or not the strata column is a predictor. On the skeptic's fixture the p-value is now 0.28 and r is 0.000. Over 1,000 null replicates through the app's own path (design_spec → build_pipeline → Linear.coefficients), p > 0.05 in 98.6% of replicates (99.0% of the first 200). The largest |r(fat_adj, sex)| is 1.7e-15, and the mean estimate is −0.42 Monte Carlo SE from 0.

Other changes:
- StratifiedEnergyAdjuster now lives in turbotab/core/methods/energy.py; models/steps.py re-exports it.
- A level with fewer than 30 fitting rows (the old floor was 3), or with constant energy, uses the pooled slope but stays centered on its own means.
- Rows with a blank strata value form their own level.
- A row from a level not seen in fit uses the pooled regression.
- The lineage formula and params report:
  - pooled r(N_adj, E), and r(N_adj, E) within each level;
  - pooled r(N_adj, strata), as the correlation ratio η;
  - r with each level's indicator;
  - each level's slope and row count;
  - which levels fall back to the pooled slope.
- The design warnings name the levels that fall back.
- NUTRITION_PACK line 480 now agrees with line 446, and the correction is recorded inline.
- With strata, the methods sentence says the added mean is over all training rows.

WP5 is fixed, committed (2104204, on turbotab-next 88d22aa), and all four §5 acceptance tests pass. The worktree branch had been cut from main, so I reset it to turbotab-next (it had no changes) before starting.

The band (MA-12). Each refit used to draw from one fixed 2,000-row subsample, and the band was the percentiles of 50 refits. Now each refit resamples every row the model was fit on, keeping a person's rows together when rows repeat, up to BAND_ROWS = 10,000. Above that, a refit draws 10,000 rows and the spread is scaled by √(m/n) (an m-out-of-n bootstrap; Bickel, Götze & van Zwet 1997). This holds for both the model fit and the averaging over the curve's rows, which are a subset of the training rows.
- The default band is the curve ± 1.96 standard errors of 200 refits (Efron & Tibshirani: a standard error rarely needs more than 200).
- With 1,000 refits or more the band uses percentiles of the refits (Carpenter & Bithell 2000). MAX_BOOT rises from 500 to 2,000 so that can be requested.
- On the real NHANES export the default band is estimated at about 175 s for three families. The old 50 refits on 2,000 rows took about 25 s.

The refits (B16 and three related problems I found).
- A family's band is drawn only if at least 90% of its refits succeed (a stated convention).
- The server writes the band's caption: rows used, refits, how they were resampled, and how many succeeded per family. The saved figure and the on-screen note now show it word for word.
- Rows with a missing ID were never drawn into a resample; each is now its own unit.
- In an elastic-net refit, copies of the same row could land on both sides of an internal tuning split. They now stay together.
- A boosted-trees refit now keeps the full fit's early-stopping choice. scikit-learn turns early stopping on only above 10,000 rows, so 10,000-row refits of a larger fit had run all 100 trees (vs 23 with early stopping, measured on 10,001 noise rows).

The support (MA-13, B17).
- When the total-energy column is a model input, a row also drops out at a given k if a moved nutrient's share of energy leaves the range observed for that share. The curve reports, at every k, how many rows each check removed.
- A fixed-population curve (the same rows at every k the curve reached) now comes with each model, along with its own band.

Limit found on real data. On NHANES the share check removes 0 extra rows at every k (at most 1 after excluding intakes outside 500–5,000 kcal). Real recall days cover almost the whole range: fat 0.000–0.704 of energy, carbohydrate 0.062–0.989. In the raw export, the near-zero kcal row (5.4×10⁻⁷⁹) produces a fat share of 9.0. So min–max support is driven by outliers, for amounts and shares alike. A joint density or distance check is the stronger fix, but it needs a threshold ruling; it is in the inbox.

Both seal guards are in place and tested through the real server. All 9 new acceptance tests pass, and all 9 fail when run against the unchanged code (88d22aa), so they detect the defects.

RO-02, the guard after the split: once rows are held out (holdout > 0), any answer that would change what the held-out draw reads is refused with a 409 `sealed`, and the last exit is always the re-seal (a revert of the split decision). That covers a new outcome, a different task, a chronological split request, a repair that rewrites the outcome, the unit column or the time column, withdrawing such a repair (defer or dismiss), and a revert that undoes any of these. For a set-to-missing repair on the outcome, the first exit is "Exclude those rows instead": it takes the impossible-value rows out of the analysis and moves no held-out row. A repair to a predictor is still accepted.

The Router now does the impossibility and code repairs before the split. The split question waits for the findings stage. Drawing the split is refused (409 `settle_first`) while a finding whose repair would rewrite a column the draw reads has not been repaired or kept. The exits are the finding's own repairs and "Keep the values as they are", which records a dismissal.

RO-01, eligibility on the outcome: any eligibility rule on the outcome is refused under both purposes (409 `rule_on_outcome`). This includes a range set by the outcome's own levels, choosing as the outcome a column that already has a rule, and a revert that would put a rule on the outcome. The exits are: drop the rule, the impossible-values or code repairs for the outcome (only those that would be accepted now), and "restrict by a variable measured before the outcome". The exclusions preview never draws the outcome's histogram, even for a rule recorded before this guard existed.

Measured on the audit's own table, replayed draw for draw (verified equal to the auditors' generated CSV): 0 of 200 held-out rows moved, compared as sets from the split's parquet on disk. deviations: Cross-package semantic fix (WP2×WP3): test_wp3 'the null holds with sex in the model too' compared the app's p with classical OLS. After WP2, the app reports HC3 on t(n−p) for independent rows. The reference p is now HC3, written out from its definition in numpy and scipy (statsmodels would not be independent of WP2's engine). The classical p is still asserted null, and the estimate check is unchanged.

Cross-package code merge (WP4×WP5): the band refit uses pinned_to_full_fit (WP5) and then inner_cv.fit_pipeline (WP4), not WP5's with_grouped_inner_cv plus pipe.fit. Boosted trees' early-stopping rows in a refit are therefore drawn by resampled row or unit too. WP5's spy test was retargeted to with_inner_cv, and a new test pins the combined path.
Cross-package test fix (WP1×GUARDS): the RO-01 exit's kept age rule now serializes WP1's ExclusionRule.missing ('exclude'). The expected dict gained that field; the guard's behavior is unchanged.

row_previews: GUARDS' choice of which rule to draw used a dict keyed by rule index, so under WP1's flow only the last line per rule counted. It now ranks by WP1's rule_drops, which sums the not-recorded, not-screened and range lines. Every rule emits its range step, so positions equal rule indices.

The clean WP1 and WP2 merge commits did not trigger the pre-commit hook (git runs it only when a conflicted merge is concluded). The later merge commits ran all six gates, and I ran the hook on the final HEAD; all pass. --no-verify was never used.

The acceptance statuses marked 'deviated' (WP2.3, WP3.2) carry the packages' own documented deviations: CR2 with Bell–McCaffrey df in place of t(G−1), and indicator r with η in place of an undefined per-level r. Neither was changed at integration.
Nothing was pushed. turbotab-next is 12 commits ahead of origin/turbotab-next.

Every missing-ID row joins one 'nan' unit in the time ranking, while WP2 counts each as its own unit. One shared key function would close this.

From WP2: the covariance is chosen by the engine. There is no user decision offering classical, HC3, CR1/t(G−1), CR2 or wild cluster bootstrap with 'customary' and 'sound' labels (North star 5). Intervals are still on training rows only (ruling 3, ME-12/WP8). Multinomial separation is not detected.

From WP4: the pooled R²'s nested-CV SE is not implemented (ME-10/WP9). The outer folds and outer CV R² still depend on file order through row-id keys (0.302 against 0.288). Elastic net's fit-time estimate is left on the one-pass-per-cell rule.

They are reachable through the API and refusal exits. Under 'change', a covariate recorded every visit, such as age, is differenced unless overridden.

From GUARDS: membership by identity and the 're-sealed after fits were seen' statement remain for WP16 proper. The optional attested block-and-record route for disease-definition restrictions is not offered.

verdicts.reasoning: I read test_wp1_data_identity.py tests 1 and 1b. Their references are pandas parses with explicit %m/%d/%Y and %d/%m/%Y formats and an ISO-copy median gap, not engine output. I re-ran it through my own server (port 8918, fresh TURBOTAB_HOME, 2 workers) on new fixtures: 2,000 coarsened US dates (seed 5) and 160 people × 3 quarterly US-format visits (seed 21). The 2,000-date column stayed VARCHAR with a 'month-first and day-first' ingest warning, and 0 of 2,000 values changed (pandas: 1,810 would move under day-first). An ambiguous_dates finding appeared with exactly three examples under each reading. After applying its month_first option, the structure reading equalled the ISO copy's (time_points, median 92 days; my pandas reference on the ISO text: 92).

The tests' references are pandas sorts by a mapped label order, an explicit '%b %d, %Y' parse, and dated records only. My server fixture had 40 people with month_12/baseline/month_6 shuffled per person. With the structure stage fresh, set_aggregation(change) got 409 cannot_order, 'Declare the order of the levels', and an exit offering baseline, month_6, month_12. Once declared, every LDL change equalled pandas last-minus-first (+4.0, max abs diff 0), and the receipt read ordered_by=visit, order='declared levels'. My graph fixtures confirmed first/last/change exclude undated records and count them. Caveat (minor): posted while the aggregation question was still 'waiting' on the structure stage, the decision was accepted without this validator. The working stage then errored with the same StructureError, so no file-order number was produced.

The tests' references are pandas transposes of the sample block, and the preview is compared cell by cell with the stage output. I re-ran through the real stage graph on my own fixtures. A compound/kegg/mz/rt export with 9 samples turned into exactly 9 sample rows, with features and values identical to pandas .T, and kegg, mz and rt kept as annotations in the features file. A numeric gene_id matrix (60 random IDs, 7 samples) kept the IDs as feature names, with no row_N renaming and label_column=gene_id. The MZmine case and the preview-equals-stage check pass in the suite.

The tests' references are plain pandas groupbys, including a first-seen mode. On my 50-person × 4-visit fixture, under 'change' the constant sex_code kept its values (1 and 2, never 0) and the smoking code got rule 'first'. Under 'mean' smoking was combined by mode (always a level from {1,2,3}, never fractional) and weight equalled the pandas mean. The receipt listed every varying numeric column with its rule, plus constant_columns=1. Residual, outside the test: a covariate that varies within a person (age at each visit) still becomes elapsed time under 'change'. The receipt shows this and a per-column rule can override it. Whole-number count columns with ≤10 levels, each seen about 3 or more times, are treated as codes (mode under 'mean').

The test's reference is pd.get_dummies with the first level dropped. I checked the user-facing fit through my server: RIDRETH3 drawn from {1,2,3,4,6,7}, glucose dependent on it. The roles stage proposed RIDRETH3 as categorical (high confidence, 'An NHANES coded variable'). After set_categorical, the inference coefficient table had exactly five indicator rows, RIDRETH3_2/3/4/6/7. Each estimate equalled statsmodels' smf.ols('glucose ~ C(RIDRETH3) + age') to every printed digit.

The tests quote the SAS source and use pandas to_numeric(errors='coerce') as the reference. On my server fixture (1,500 rows, 4% '.' in age, 2% '.' plus 'NA.' in kcal, 8% '<0.3' in crp), age and kcal ingested as VARCHAR. text_numbers findings named every spelling with counts ('`.` (`34`), `NA.` (`3`)'). After read_numbers, the working table equalled pandas' coercion exactly (float64). '<0.3' produced a separate below_detection__crp finding with half_limit and limit_root2 options. My own ';'-separated decimal-comma file read to numbers identical to its dot-decimal copy (pandas reference).

The test asserts parity over the app's own NULL_TOKENS, as the spec says to. As an independent list I used 23 spellings: pandas' default NA strings plus 'None', 'none', 'NONE', '.', 'Missing'. I saved them as CSV and xlsx and ingested both through my server. Missing counts agreed column for column, with zero disagreements. 'None' stayed an answer in both (0 missing).

The test's reference is numpy over the finite values. Through my server (fiber_per_1000 with two zero-kcal days), the profile completed. The served summary reported n_infinite=2, and its mean, SD, min and max matched numpy over the finite values to about 1e-15. An infinite_values finding said '`2` cells … are infinite' and offered set_missing. On my own frame with +inf, −inf and NaN, the DuckDB and Arrow summaries agreed with each other and with numpy (type-7 quartiles) to a relative error of 1.3e-15, and both counted 3 infinities.

The test quotes STROBE 13(a) and uses pandas counts as the reference. My own cohort_flow fixture had 2,000 rows with 25% of age missing and the rule age 18–65. It produced a separate step, '`age` not recorded', dropping 465 (pandas: 465), and '`age` within `18`–`65`' with n=827 (pandas: 827). The by-sex screen (D16) on my fixture reported '`kcal` not screened: no range for its `sex`' dropping 66 (pandas: 66). It kept 892, equal to the pandas count, and no 9,500 kcal day survived.

The test's references are statsmodels OLS and CR1 on the same rows, against the analytic truth of 0. I re-ran 400 replicates per grain through the real stage graph (GraphRun, holdout 0, my own seeds, 'participant_id'). Coverage was 0.9625 for grain unknown (basis undetermined) and 0.935 for one-row-each (basis abandoned), against plain OLS at 0.82 (MC SE 0.011). On 40 replicates each, the app's SE and df equalled my own CR2/Bell–McCaffrey implementation (scipy sqrtm, eigenvalues of the n×n form) to 1e-9. Default-role server run: participant_id proposed as identifier, CR2, SE equal to mine. Residual, user-facing: names the role proposer misses ('pid', 'patient', 'eid' come out as 'exposure', an IN-06 gap) get HC3, not clustering. That happens even though structure.grain.suggested names the column. The concern then says 'no identifier repeats' (server: SE 0.0345 against 0.0489 under CR2).

The test drives the real server and uses statsmodels MixedLM as the reference. I rebuilt the E/scenA.py 6×40 null-sodium fixture and drove my own uvicorn server. The seal basis was abandoned. Inference covariance was 'none' with n_clusters=6, and the refusal cited the 8-unit floor. Every coefficient row had p, ci_low and ci_high null. The exits were 'Combine each `participant_id`'s rows into one' and 'A random-intercept mixed model or GEE (not yet in TurboTab)'. References on the same rows: MixedLM p=0.852, naive OLS p=4.1e-14.

Documented deviation: the engine uses CR2 with Bell–McCaffrey (BM) df instead of a literal t(9). That is the audit's own recommendation and Cameron & Miller's 'best methods use the CR2VE and T(v*)'. My independent CR2/BM code matched the engine's SE, df, CI and p to 7e-13 on 60 random unbalanced designs. BM df never exceeded G−1 there, and at most 1.00004×(G−1) over 200 adversarial designs. So the intervals are never materially narrower than t(G−1); at G=10 the half-width/SE was 2.80 against t(9)=2.262. My own MC (unbalanced 5–35 rows per cluster, heteroskedastic, G=12) gave type-I 0.057 (OLS, 1,500 reps) and 0.053 (logistic, 800 reps), against CR1-z at 0.137 and 0.115. A 'G = …' concern appears below 30. Minor: the caption names CR2, G and 'Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom' but not the df number, which is per row.

The tests' references are statsmodels' classical and HC3 fits and a hand-computed Koenker Breusch–Pagan. My own MC at n=200, null slope, lognormal intake, 2,000 reps: with SD proportional to intake, app coverage 0.9275 (≥0.92) against classical 0.61. With variance proportional to intake, 0.937 against 0.80. The app's SE equalled my hand-written HC3 to 1e-9, and the caption reads 'HC3 … on t(n−p)'. The residual-spread concern fired on 394/400 heteroskedastic fits and 1/400 homoskedastic ones.

The tests' references are a generic-optimizer Firth fit and Haldane's closed form. On the audit's 20 seeds (A-skeptic/s14b fixture), the separated column was named on all 20 and the table was Firth's. Estimates agreed with my own L-BFGS Firth to 2.5e-7 and p to 2e-8. On three seeds my optimizer's lower bound differed by up to 0.025. Checking with a robust profile maximizer showed the app's bound gives 2×drop=3.841459 exactly, so the app was right and my optimizer was off. Through my server, the exposure row read Firth 5.366 (mine 5.366038) with a profile CI and a likelihood-ratio p, and the concern named `exposed`; maximum-likelihood Logit would have printed 31.2 with p≈1.0.

The test counts units by hand and checks a bijection with the split's mapping, which the spec requires. On my graph fixture (40 people × 4 rows, 20 IDs blanked), the app reported n_clusters=60 (mine: 40+20=60), matching the split's 60 groups. Its CR2 SE and df equalled my implementation with each blank as its own unit (0.0938249 and 25.6243). The shared-code mapping gives a different SE (0.0961). The caption says '20 rows with no `participant_id` counted as units of their own'.

The test's references are the analytic null and numpy polyfit, with a positive control. I ran 400 replicates through the real graph (GraphRun) on my own variant: 45% male, different energy and fat distributions, sex excluded. p>0.05 in 100% of replicates (min 0.051), max |r(fat_adj, sex)| 3.9e-15, mean estimate −5e-6 (MC SE 2e-4). The app's estimate equalled OLS on my own within-sex-residual-plus-cohort-mean algebra to 1e-15. The audit's B-skeptic/s1_strata.py run on the fixed code: p=0.28 (was 1e-106), r=0.000 (was 0.56).

The test's reference is an analytic E[MSE] target (0.1345), plus sklearn per-fold R² for the old estimator. Each expected value comes from a separate path (pandas or numpy, statsmodels, sklearn, scipy, closed forms, or truth fixed by the data-generating process), and the tests that deviate from the spec say so in their docstrings. The suites pass: 92 acceptance tests in 86 s, and 833 more in turbotab/core plus turbotab/server in 128 s. I did not commit; all scratch work is under /private/tmp/turbotab-fix/verify/.

How I reproduced the numbers: my own uvicorn servers on ports 8917–8923, each with a fresh TURBOTAB_HOME and 2 workers, plus the real stage graph (GraphRun), on new fixtures and seeds. References were my own implementations in /private/tmp/turbotab-fix/verify/indep.py: CR2 via sqrtm, Bell–McCaffrey df via eigenvalues, and Firth via L-BFGS. I also re-ran several of the audit's repro scripts. Headline numbers:
- Repeated-rows coverage: 0.9625 and 0.935, against OLS 0.82.
- 6×40 case: intervals refused; mixed-model p 0.852, naive p 4e-14.

§6 regression re-check found nothing broken: AUC with the declared event and flip invariance (against an exact maximum-likelihood reference), baseline AUC 0.5, grouped and stratified, deterministic splits, elastic-net back-transform, multinomial row alignment with CR2, Hanley–McNeil 0.0564, energy-residual identities, the refusal of log residuals on zeros, Atwater 4/4/9/7/2, nested substitution arithmetic, aggregation basics with continuous values, ZIP/FIPS and a leading zero at row 35,000 staying text, Excel '001' staying text, 1.5 million-row row identity, and the flow step excluding ±inf.

An ID named 'pid', 'patient' or 'eid' is proposed as an exposure, so intervals fall back to HC3 even though structure.grain.suggested names that column. The concern then says 'no identifier repeats'.
